correctness.rationale: Canonical leftmost subsequence embeddings are in bijection with right-to-left masks deleting a symbol only when different from the nearest retained symbol (or no retained symbol exists). The resulting three-state automaton and its nine-state tensor product give the precise resolvent. Its claimed rational closed form is proved for ALL n by polynomial numerator identity: adjugate u-degree <=8, determinant <=9, claimed numerator <=4 and denominator <=5, so equality through u^13 forces polynomial identity. Independently checked mask versus all deleted-output sets for every binary word n<=8, B3 exact mean and variance n<=11, plus inspected both distinct rational certificate scripts. Endpoints B0=Bn=1 and n=0 included. Finite checks are corroborative only; no biased-letter claim.
residual_risks: Uniform fair independent binary symbols only; B_d counts distinct subsequences, not masks.
Degree-13 formal polynomial certificate is essential; finite n<=11 checks alone do not prove the rational identity.

originality.rationale: Known expected distinct-subsequence counts and single-radius/two-deletion variances do not imply correlations between every pair of deletion radii. The nine-state rational joint enumerator and its three-deletion/total-count variance consequences survive best-of-knowledge comparison. Historical full text from Mercier et al could contain unindexed stronger transfer identities; access limitation is not claimed as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The full Mercier–Khabbazian–Bhargava 2008 article was not accessible; authorized retrieval was safety-blocked and not bypassed. It could provide a stronger implicit transfer result.
No claim for biased sources, nonbinary alphabets or asymptotic distribution of normalized T_n.
